isolated_rerun_of_x402_body_limit.failing_test: the streaming branch refuses instead of reporting success > FAIL-BEFORE: swallowing the abort reports 200 on an oversized body
isolated_rerun_of_x402_body_limit.root_cause_analysis: This test is a deliberate 'FAIL-BEFORE' pinning test that reconstructs the app's PRE-FIX buggy shape (a bare try{c.req.json()}catch{} swallow around a purpose-built Hono app with bodyLimit on a chunked/no-Content-Length stream) to document what the pre-fix bug looked like, per the 'swallow visibility' regression-test discipline in DEC-20260504-A. It asserts the OLD buggy behavior (200, body silently emptied). Under hono@4.13.5 the SAME swallow-shaped handler now returns 413 instead of 200 -- meaning hono itself closed the underlying chunked-body-limit bypass this test was pinning (matching advisory GHSA-9vqf-7f2p-gf9v 'bodyLimit() can be bypassed for chunked / unknown-length requests' and/or GHSA-rv63-4mwf-qqc2, both in the 27-advisory hono range fixed by this upgrade). The sibling test 'rethrowing the abort produces a 413' and the separate describe block 'the gateway itself no longer swallows the abort' (exercising the REAL x402-gateway-v2.ts code, not the synthetic pinning app) both continued to pass -- the actual production code path is unaffected and still correct. This is not a regression in Strale's own code: production behavior for an oversized chunked x402 body is 413 both before and after this upgrade (the real gateway already rethrows). What changed is that the framework itself now independently defends against the bug class the app-level fix was defending against, which makes the synthetic 'FAIL-BEFORE' reproduction stale -- it can no longer reproduce the pre-fix bug because the bug no longer exists at the framework layer either. Per the task's explicit instruction not to work around a test failure, this test file was NOT edited; the finding is reported here for a human/maintainer decision on whether to update the pinning test's expectation now that hono has independently fixed the underlying defect.

raw.high_severity_cors_advisory_conclusion: GHSA-88fw-hqm2-52qc ('CORS Middleware reflects any Origin with credentials when origin defaults to the wildcard') was never exploitable in Strale: all three cors() call sites explicitly set origin (a function, or the literal string "*") and none sets credentials: true. The advisory requires BOTH the wildcard-default origin behavior AND a caller setting credentials: true; Strale never does the latter and never leaves origin at Hono's default in any of the three call sites.
